title: 1966 AHSME Problem 16
statement:
If

\[ \begin{gathered} \dfrac{4^x}{2^{x+y}}=8,\\ \dfrac{9^{x+y}}{3^{5y}}=243, \end{gathered} \]

\(x\) and \(y\) are real numbers, then \(xy\) equals:

solutions.text:
The first equation becomes \(2^{x-y}=2^3,\) so \(x-y=3.\) The second becomes \(3^{2x-3y}=3^5,\) so \(2x-3y=5.\) Solving gives \(y=1,\) \(x=4,\) and hence \(xy=4.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Rewrite both equations with bases \(2\) and \(3\)
Equate exponents to obtain two linear equations in \(x\) and \(y\)
